Perhaps by dividing the camera station into close and far from human activity (under x meters --> high human activity vice versa). messages.body_plain:
Hi,

the function activityOverlap() in camtrapR can help you. It uses the overlap package internally, but does a few steps for you (e.g. convert time to radial time). Run:

examples(activityOverlap)

to see a few examples. Please also see vignette 4 for details:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr4.html#Visualising_species_activity_data

If you wish to use overlap directly, the function in overlap is called overlapPlot.

Your table seems to contain the necessary information, even though I'm slightly confused by the start and end time columns. The function will require you to use only one time columns.

Best,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Announcement: new functionalities in camtrapR
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
I'd like to announce some major novelties in the GitHub version of camtrapR (v2.1.1).

1) there is a new function communityModel() to flexibly create community (multi-species) occupancy models for JAGS and Nimble. It will create model code, sets parameters to monitor and initial values, gathers model input data, and bundles all that in a "commOccu" object. Once can flexibly define model structure.
Furthermore there are fit(), predict(), plot_effects() and plot_coef() methods for these commOccu objects. See the new vignette 5 for examples and details:

https://jniedballa.github.io/camtrapR/articles/camtrapr5.html

It is still under development and a bit experimental, so please report back if unexpected things happen, and don't be surprised if things are still changing in the future.

2) camtrapR now supports multiple hierarchy levels in species tags. See "Cat" below:

I hope this will give you more freedom and can help keep the species list tidy compared to the previous restriction to a tag structure like this:

The old structure will still work like before though and you don't need to change anything in your existing code. I have not yet tested it with individual IDs.

On a side note, each tag can have a custom icon as in the first example above. This can be done in the Tag manager, but is not valid outside digiKam and the icons will not be saved in the metadata. But it might be helpful in tagging images

3) the new version uses static vignettes, so installation from GitHub is now via:

install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", build_vignettes = TRUE)

I hope I can push this to CRAN early next year.

Wishing you all a happy holiday season!

Jürgen

messages.subject: Help with independent records
messages.body_plain:
Hello Everyone!!!!

I´m new using camtrapR and I have a question about independent records. I have this data of camera trap on csv format with the next information: station, Species, Date, Time, DateTimeOriginal and sampling event. In the past I have extracted independent records with the same kind of information using the next R code succesfully :

library(camtrapR)

base <- read.csv2 ("paisaje12021.csv", header = TRUE)
head(base)
names(base)

#################### filter records 24H
records_filter24_h <- camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence(intable = base,
                                                              deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord",
                                                              columnOfInterest = "Species",
                                                              stationCol = "Station",
                                                              minDeltaTime = 1440,
                                                              camerasIndependent = FALSE )

But now I'm using again this code and it fails to extract independent records and I have no idea why. At the begining I thought it was the format on the  DateTime Original column, but I think the format is correct and I run out of Ideas how to fix it. I'd appreciate any advice on this.
Thanks
Sorry for my english
